key_insight: Data-free continuous-time PINNs reproduce cylinder vortex shedding, while enforcing pressure continuity and a hidden incompressibility constraint improves consistency across training windows.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports reference-data-free prediction of unsteady cylinder wakes and reduces artificial jumps in lift at time-window boundaries.
method: Train continuous-time PINNs over successive time windows at Re=100, without reference data or temporal discretization.
Break wake symmetry using an analytical, divergence-free initial velocity field.
Impose junction pressure and add the hidden constraint ∇·∂ₜv=0 to the loss.
evidence_signal: Strouhal number and mean drag agree within 0.5% of an OpenFOAM solution on the same domain; the consistency remedy reduces lift jumps 20-fold over five shedding periods.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported Re=100 cylinder case; robustness across other Reynolds numbers, geometries, and longer time horizons remains unestablished.
paper_title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
